increment: Compiler work budget and live charge callback; runtime charging still pending
method: Same-host serial release runs without concurrent builds/tests. Baseline archived to separate source/target. Identical legacy performance fixture (one warmup, three measured, median). New API within-candidate comparison (one warmup, five measured, median), source construction and output equality excluded; callback meter destruction included. Admission one warmup plus seven measured. Final after run includes the reviewed using-scan charge.
limitations: No legacy-path speedup claim: baseline and candidate both had noisy failing runs, retained below. Final baseline branch growth 2.535x fails the unchanged 2.5x gate; final candidate passes.

Budgeted and callback paths add intentional compilation charges under ironhorse-compile-meter-1; legacy raw=0 in new fixture means no host bill, not zero token telemetry. Legacy parse computrons remain identical in paired controls.
New API modes compare within this candidate, not APIs available in baseline. At 32k branches callback median is about 7% above legacy in reviewed run; no statistical-significance claim.
Admission timings near timer resolution only demonstrate pre-allocation refusal, not a precise nanosecond cost or meaningful speedup ratio.
Conservative reservations can overcharge simple long regexps and BigInts; cost units are deterministic policy, not calibrated CPU time.
VM eval, Function, and daemon compilation still need wiring to this API before F065 is complete.
